titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 15, the hymns (part 1 of 4)
part: Spell 15 — the hymns, part 1 of 4: a hymn to Ra at his rising and the opening of a hymn to Osiris (Plates 18–19)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plates XVIII, XIX. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 123–127; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: Spell 15 is a set of hymns sung to the sun and to Osiris; on Ani's papyrus it comes after Spell 10 on Plate 18 and runs on across Plate 19. This first part holds a hymn to Ra as he rises, spoken by Ani: the sun crosses the sky in his two barks, the stars praise him, his enemy is bound and cut down, and he is hailed as the one god who spoke the world out of silence. It ends with Ani's titles, and then a second hymn begins, to Osiris as lord of eternity, whom the sun's setting brings to the dead. Several signs in Budge's type are uncertain, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: adoring · Ra · at · rising · his · in · the-horizon · until · coming-about · setting · his · in · life
sentences.i: Adoring Ra at his rising in the horizon until his setting comes about, in life.
sentences.n: Spell 15 begins, and the papyrus writes its title in red, except the name of Ra and ꜣḫt 'horizon', which stand in black. dwꜣ 'adore, praise' is the star (dwꜣ) with the vulture ꜣ as complement, a standing man raising his arm in worship (approximated in the type) and the papyrus roll; as in the hymn on Plate 1 it is the infinitive, naming the act: 'adoring Ra'. rꜥ 'Ra' is written here with the seated god wearing the sun-disk alone. m wbn·f 'at his rising': after the preposition m, wbn 'rise' (quail chick w, foot b, water n, the sun as classifier) is the infinitive, and the suffix ·f 'his', the horned viper, is its subject. ꜣḫt 'horizon' is the sun between two hills, with t as complement and a house-like sign as classifier. r ḫpr ḥtp·f: r 'to' with the infinitive ḫpr 'come about' (scarab ḫpr, r as complement), whose subject is ḥtp·f 'his setting' (offering table ḥtp with t and p as complements, and ·f): 'to the coming about of his setting', that is, until he sets; ḥtp is 'be at peace, rest', and of the sun 'set'. m ꜥnḫ 'in life' (ankh with n and ḫ as complements): the sun goes down alive, to rise again. Spell 15 is a set of hymns to the sun and to Osiris; this is the first of them.

sentences.i: Said by the Osiris, the scribe Ani:
sentences.n: ḏd in N 'said by N', in red, brings in the speaker. ḏd 'say' is the cobra ḏ and the hand d, printed as one ligature; in 'by', which names the one who speaks, is the reed i over the water n. sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · Ra · in · rising · his · Atum · Horakhty
sentences.i: Hail to you, Ra, in his rising, Atum-Horakhty!
sentences.n: Ani's speech begins, in black. Budge prints ind-ḥr·k as one group; it is split here into the interjection and ḥr·k. ind 'hail, greetings' is the reed i and a post with a knobbed top and a side arm (the sign nḏ, Aa27, approximated in the type), with the papyrus roll; ḥr·k is the face ḥr with its stroke and the basket ·k 'you, your': literally 'greetings to your face'. rꜥ 'Ra' is the seated god with the sun-disk. m wbn·f 'in his rising' as in the title, here with the sun shedding rays (N8, approximate) as classifier: the god is greeted and then spoken of in the third person, as often in hymns. itm 'Atum' is the loaf t and the sledge tm (U15) with the seated god; the reed i of the name is not written (Budge: Tem). The falcon ḥr with two rounded oblongs each crossed by a stroke (coded N18 twice, an approximation; Budge reads χuti) is taken, with Budge, as ḥr-ꜣḫty 'Horakhty', 'Horus of the horizon', the doubled sign standing for the horizon; Budge prints Ḥeru and χuti apart, and they are joined here as one name. Atum is the sun as the old creator, Horakhty the sun standing above the horizon: one god under his names.

sentences.i: Praise to you! Your beauty is in my eyes, and radiance comes to be upon (my) breast.
sentences.n: Budge prints dwꜣ-tw as one group; it is split here into the verb and tw 'you', the dependent pronoun (loaf t, quail chick w) that stands as the object. dwꜣ is the star with ꜣ as complement, a kneeling man with an arm raised (approximated) and the papyrus roll; no subject follows, so it is taken as the infinitive used as an exclamation, 'adoring you', 'praise to you'. The construction is not certain: in older Egyptian an infinitive takes a pronoun object as a suffix (as ḥr dwꜣ·k in line 10), and a dependent tw after it is a later usage. Budge takes it as a passive, 'adored art thou'; the sense comes to the same. nfrw·k 'your beauty' is the heart-and-windpipe nfr written three times, the plural used for an abstract noun, and ·k. m irty·i 'in my two eyes': the eye written twice is irty, the dual of irt 'eye', and the seated man is ·i 'my'; no sickle is printed, so the word is 'eyes', not mꜣꜣ 'see' (Budge reads maa-à). nfrw·k m irty·i is a sentence with no verb, 'your beauty (is) in my eyes'. ḫpr ꜣḫw is a sḏm·f with a noun subject, 'radiance comes into being': ꜣḫw 'radiance, sunlight' is the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ as complement, w, the sun shedding rays (approximate) and a stroke. ḥr šnbt 'upon the breast': ḥr is the face with its stroke, here the preposition 'upon'; šnbt 'breast' is the cord-loop šn (V7, approximate) with n, foot b, t and a fleshy curl (F51, approximate). No 'my' is written; Budge supplies it. The worshipper stands in the morning light and feels it on his body.

sentences.i: You go on your way in your peace in the Sektet-bark;
sentences.n: wḏꜣ·k 'you proceed' is the quail chick w, a tall tapering sign taken as the fire-drill ḏꜣ (U28, approximate) and the walking legs, then ·k: the sḏm·f of wḏꜣ 'go on, set out'. m ḥtp·k 'in your peace': ḥtp (offering table, t, p) as a noun, with ·k; since ḥtp is also the sun's 'setting', 'at your setting' is possible, and Budge too was unsure of the ·k ('peace thy'). m sktt 'in the Sektet-bark' (Budge: sektet): the bolt s, the basket k, two loaves t and a boat with a cabin (approximated). The Sektet is the bark in which the sun travels; in these hymns it is paired with the Adjet-bark of the next line.

sentences.l: heart · your · is-glad · in · the-fair-wind · in · the-Adjet-bark · heart · its · is-sweet
sentences.i: your heart is glad with the fair wind in the Adjet-bark, and its heart is pleased.
sentences.n: ib·k ꜣw 'your heart is glad': ib is the heart with its stroke and ·k; ꜣw 'long, extended' is a hatched block on an arch with hanging cords (the spine sign ꜣw, F40, approximate), with w as complement and the papyrus roll, the stative after a noun subject. 'Long of heart' is the Egyptian way of saying glad. m mꜣꜥw 'with the fair wind': the sickle mꜣ, a low flat sign that this type prints where ꜥ is read (coded U15), w, a sail as the classifier of wind (approximate), the curl w again and plural strokes; mꜣꜥw is the wind that blows right for the boat, from mꜣꜥ 'true, right' (Budge: maāu, 'winds'). m ꜥḏt 'in the Adjet-bark' (Budge: āṭet) is the netting-needle sign ꜥḏ (V26, approximate) with the hand d, two t's and a boat, as on Plate 1; Budge's line numeral 4 is printed inside the word. ib·s nḏm 'its heart is sweet': ib·s is the heart with the bolt ·s 'its', the bark (a feminine noun); nḏm 'be sweet, pleasant' is printed with the same braided sign as the wick ḥ (coded V28, approximate) where the pod nḏm is expected, then m as complement and the roll; Budge reads net'em. The sun's boats sail on a wind that never fails.

sentences.i: (You) cross the sky in peace;
sentences.n: nmi 'traverse, travel across' is water n as complement, a slanting rod taken as the knife nm (T34, approximate), the owl m as complement and the reed i, then two classifiers: a square meander-like sign (coded O38, an approximation; it has no clear value) and the walking legs. No subject is written: Budge supplies [k] in his transliteration only, and the same words in line 8 have ·k. The suffix may have been left out, as often; the reading shows only what is printed, and the translation supplies '(you)'. ḥrt 'the sky' is the face ḥr with r, t and the sign of the sky. m ḥtpw 'in peace' is the offering table with t and p, two reeds, w and a stroke; the two reeds are not part of the usual spelling and are not read, with Budge (ḥetepu).

sentences.n: sḫr 'fell, overthrow' is the causative s- of ḫr 'fall': bolt s, placenta ḫ, mouth r and a man falling forward (approximated), then the low flat sign U15, here a classifier and not read. With a noun subject and no agent it is taken as the passive sḏm·f, 'are felled'. ḫftyw·k 'your enemies': placenta ḫ, viper f, loaf t and the vulture ꜣ, a kneeling man with an arm raised (the enemy, approximated), a small circle and plural strokes, then ·k. The vulture stands where the y of ḫfty is expected and is not read (Budge: χefta). The sun's enemies are struck down as he travels.

sentences.n: Budge prints hnw-n·k as one group; it is split here into hnw and n·k 'to you, for you' (water n and ·k). hnw 'jubilation, praise' is the shelter h, water n, the pot nw with w as complement and a kneeling man raising both arms (approximated), with a stroke; it is taken as a sḏm·f, 'they jubilate', with the short n·k before the noun subject, as short words go in Egyptian; as a noun it would give 'jubilation to you'. They are the stars that never stop moving, the planets and the stars that rise and set.

sentences.n: dwꜣ tw iḫmw-sk is built like dwꜣ tw ḥryw on Plate 1: verb, the pronoun tw 'you' as object, and the noun subject. Budge prints dwꜣ-tw as one group; it is split here. dwꜣ is the star with the standing worshipper (approximated) and the roll. iḫmw-sk 'the Imperishable Stars', 'those who do not know perishing', joins two of Budge's words: iḫm is written with the owl m before the placenta ḫ this time, and sk 'perish' is the bolt s as complement, a braided sign that the type prints like the wick ḥ (coded V28, approximate) where the sign sk (V29) is expected, the basket k as complement, a star and a stroke. They are the stars round the pole that never set. ḥtp 'setting' has no subject written; Budge supplies [thou]. It is taken as the stative, the form that describes a state, with its ending unwritten: '(you) being set', 'as you set'. ḥtp is the offering table with t and p; Budge's numeral 6 stands before it. m ꜣḫt nt mꜣnw 'in the horizon of Manu': nt is the genitive 'of' in its feminine form, agreeing with ꜣḫt; mꜣnw 'Manu' is the sickle mꜣ with the pot nw written three times and the hill-country sign, the mountain of the west where the sun goes down.

sentences.i: You are beautiful in the Two Shrines(?), O lord, living and enduring as my lord.
sentences.n: nfr·ṯi 'you are beautiful' is the heart-and-windpipe nfr with the tethering rope ṯ, the stative with its ending ·ṯi 'you' written short (the reed of ·ṯi is left out); Budge prints nefer-θà. ꜥnḫ·ṯi 'you are living' is the ankh with the same ending. The stative describes the state its subject is in. The next word is two dotted disks stacked (N5 N5); Budge reads àterti with his own query and gives 'the two halves of the sky'. It is read here, with the same doubt, as itrty 'the Two Shrines', the shrines of the south and the north that stand for the whole land; no sound sign is written, and another word for 'the two (times, days)' may lie behind the two suns. nb 'lord' (the basket) is an address. ḏd 'stable, enduring' is the djed pillar written twice, the second as classifier: the stative of ḏd 'be stable', with its ending unwritten; Budge reads ṭeṭṭeṭ. m nb·i 'as my lord': m is written with Aa15, then nb with the seated god and ·i, the seated man. Living and stable is what a god or a king is wished to be for ever.

sentences.i: You rise and you shine upon the back of your mother, having appeared in glory as king of the gods.
sentences.n: wbn·k and psd·k are two sḏm·f forms, 'you rise, you shine'; in wbn·k the type prints water n before the foot b. psd 'shine' is p, the bolt s and the hand d, with a diagonal rod crossed by ribs (the backbone sign, F37, approximate) and the sun-disk as classifiers; it is spelled with the hand d where older writing has the cobra ḏ, as on Plate 1. ḥr psd mwt·k 'upon the back of your mother': psd 'back' is the same letters with the backbone as classifier, the word that the shining verb is written like; mwt is the vulture mwt with ·k. The mother is the sky-goddess Nut, whose body arches over the earth; the sun travels along her back. ḫꜥ·ṯi 'you having appeared in glory' is the stative with ·ṯi: the sun rising over a hill (N28, approximate) with the low flat sign U15 where the arm ꜥ is read as complement, the papyrus roll, the rope ṯ and the reed i. m nswt nṯrw 'as king of the gods': nswt is the sedge with t and n written after it, the usual spelling of the word, and nṯrw the flag written three times. Budge's numeral 8 stands before nṯrw.

sentences.n: ir·n nwt nyny 'Nut has made greeting': ir is the eye alone (iri 'do, make') and the water n after it is the n of the sḏm·n·f, the form of completed action, which stands before the noun subject. The Rebel is the serpent enemy of the sun.

sentences.l: his-two-arms · bound · has-cut-off · the-knife · backbone · his
sentences.i: his arms are bound, and the knife has cut through his backbone.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ꜣ-q-s-ꜣ-w and s-ḥ-q; read qꜣs 'bound' and ḥsq 'cut off'. The first verb has the vulture ꜣ before q and again after s, with the curl w and the low flat sign U15 as classifier; Plate 1 has the same phrase, ꜥwy·f qꜣs 'his arms are bound', and the letters of qꜣs are all here, out of order. The second has s and ḥ the wrong way round, with q, and then a knife and U15 as classifiers; ḥsq is the verb for cutting off with a knife. Budge reads aqesau 'cut off' and seḥeq 'severed'. ꜥwy·f 'his two arms' is the low flat sign U15 written twice with a stroke between, standing where the arm ꜥ is read (Budge āāui-f), and ·f. qꜣs is the stative after its subject. ḥsq·n is the sḏm·n·f: the water n after the verb, which Budge prints as a word of its own, is joined to it here. dmt 'knife' (Budge: ṭemt) is the hand d, Aa15 m, t and a knife, the subject. ṯst·f 'his backbone' is the tethering sign ṯs (S24) with the bolt s as complement, t, a fleshy curl (approximate), a stroke and ·f (Budge: θeset-f, 'his sinews'). The enemy of the sun is bound and butchered.

sentences.l: the-Sektet-bark · has-hauled(?) · it · reaches · him · is-towed
sentences.i: the Sektet-bark has hauled(?) and reaches him; he is towed along.
sentences.n: sktt, the Sektet-bark, now has a boat with mast and sail as classifier (approximated). It is named first and taken up again by the suffix in sk·n·s: sk is the bolt s as complement, the braided sign printed like the wick ḥ (coded V28, approximate) where the sign sk is expected, the basket k as complement and U15 as classifier, then water n and the bolt ·s 'it, she', the bark. As a sḏm·n·f, 'it has hauled'; the sense 'haul, tow' of sk is taken from Budge ('draweth on') and is not certain, and sk n·s, 'one hauls for it', is also possible. pḥ sw: pḥ 'reach, arrive' is the hindquarters of a lion (approximate) with the walking legs; sw is the sedge sw with w, the dependent pronoun 'him'. After a verb the dependent pronoun is its object, so pḥ sw is '(it) reaches him', with the bark, unwritten, still the subject; an old passive, 'he is reached', is also possible. Budge's 'he arriveth' would need sw as the subject of an active verb, which the grammar does not allow. stꜣ·tw 'he is towed' joins two of Budge's groups: stꜣ 'drag, tow' is the bolt s, t, a small cup taken for the sign tꜣ (W10, approximate), the vulture ꜣ as complement and w, with the coiled cord and the walking legs as classifiers; then t and w, the ending of the passive sḏm·tw·f. The w after ꜣ is not read. The sun's boat is hauled along by towing-ropes, as boats on the Nile were.

sentences.i: Those of the south, the north, the west and the east are adoring you.
sentences.n: Four nisbas, adjectives made from nouns with -y and used as plural nouns, 'those of the south …': šmꜥyw is a tall stem with a hooked top crossing the low flat sign U15 (the sign šmꜥ, M26, approximate; Budge's qemāiu is his old value for it), two strokes y, a small wedge, w and a stroke; mḥtyw is the papyrus-roll-and-stem sign mḥ (V22, approximate), t, the vulture ꜣ and a stroke; imntyw is the emblem of the West with t, ꜣ, a stroke and the hill-country sign; iꜣbtyw is the emblem of the East with b, two t's and the hill-country sign. In the second and third the vulture ꜣ stands for the ending (Budge: meḥtaiu, àmentaiu) and is not read; in the fourth the second t stands where the ending is expected. Budge supplies '[the gods of]'. ḥr dwꜣ·k 'are adoring you': ḥr 'upon' with an infinitive says what is going on, and ·k after the infinitive is its object. Budge's numeral 11 is printed between the roll and ·k. All the beings of the four quarters worship the sun.

sentences.l: Primeval-One · of-forms · who-sent-forth · the-voice · the-earth · flooded · with · silence
sentences.i: O Primeval One of the forms of being, who sent forth the voice while the earth lay flooded with silence;
sentences.n: pꜣwty 'the Primeval One' is a bird with wings raised, alighting (the sign pꜣ, G41, approximate), then two small dotted disks, coded as the round loaf pꜣwt (X6) by the house ruling for this word (the shape is the same as the sun-disk N5), and the seated god: the nisba of pꜣwt 'primeval time', 'he who belongs to the first time', with its ending unwritten. Budge reads pautti and gives 'the double Paut'; both disks are taken as classifiers, the loaf of pꜣwt written twice, not as a dual. ḫprw 'forms, ways of coming into being' (scarab, r, w, a standing wrapped figure, the roll and a stroke) follows directly as its genitive. wd 'who sends forth' is the chick w and the hand d with a small cross and U15 as classifiers: the participle of wdi 'put, cast, send out'. ḫrw 'the voice' is the oar ḫrw with w and the man with hand to mouth. tꜣ bꜥḥ m sgr: tꜣ 'the earth' (land with grains) and bꜥḥ 'flooded', a heron on a perch (G32, approximate), the word-sign of bꜥḥ 'flood', as a stative: 'the earth being flooded'. sgr 'silence' is the bolt s, a stand taken as the jar-stand g (W11, approximate), r and the man with hand to mouth. The creator speaks into a world still drowned in silence.

sentences.l: the-One · who-came-into-being · in(?) · the-sky · not · had-come-into-being · the-ground · the-mountains
sentences.i: the One who came into being in(?) the sky when neither the ground nor the mountains had come into being;
sentences.n: wꜥ 'the One' is the harpoon wꜥ with its stroke and U15 standing for the complement ꜥ. ḫpr 'who came into being' is the participle (scarab and r). The next word is the crossed planks im, t and w: imytw 'between, in the midst of'. Budge reads àmtu and gives 'in', and that sense is taken here, with doubt, for 'in the sky' (pt: p, t and the sky sign). n ḫpr 'had not come into being': n (the arms held apart, with water n) before a sḏm·f denies a past event. sꜣṯw 'the ground' is the pintail duck sꜣ with t (for ṯ, as later scribes often write it), a small circle (approximate) and a stroke (Budge: set, 'the earth'). ḏww 'the mountains' is the mountain sign ḏw with a low hatched sign (approximated as O31; not read) and two strokes for the plural. The two subjects stand side by side with no 'and'. The god existed before the land rose out of the waters.

sentences.n: The first word is a man walking with a stick over his shoulder (coded A33, an approximation), the curl w and U15. sentences.i: he has fashioned the tongue of the Ennead of the gods,
sentences.n: nb·n·f 'he has fashioned' is the sḏm·n·f of nbi 'fashion, mould, cast': the broad collar of gold on its stand (the sign nb, S12, approximate), foot b as complement and U15 as classifier, then n and ·f; Budge prints it as one word, nub-nef. The gold sign writes the verb because metal is cast in a mould. ns 'the tongue' is a horizontal sign with a hooked end (the tongue, F20, approximate; it is drawn like the hoe mr) with a stroke and a small curl (approximate). psḏt 'the Ennead' is a circle divided by a line, coded X6 by the house ruling for Budge's paut and close in shape to the sign psḏ (N9), with t: the company of nine gods. Budge reads paut and gives 'cycle'. nṯrw 'of the gods' follows directly as a genitive. The tongue is the organ of speech, by which the gods create.

sentences.n: pr·k 'you come forth' is the house pr with r as complement and ·k: the sḏm·f of pri. im·f 'from it' is the preposition m in its form before a suffix, written with the reed i and the owl, and ·f, referring to the water. ḥr 'upon' (face and stroke). npt is water n, a long rounded oblong (approximated as N18), p, t, a small hourglass-like sign (approximated as N23) and a stroke: Budge reads nept and gives 'the inundated land'. The Lake of Horus is a water of the sky from which the sun comes up.

sentences.n: tpi·i 'I breathe in' is t, p and the reed i with the nose (D19, approximate) as classifier, then the seated man ·i: the sḏm·f of a verb tpi 'breathe, inhale' (Budge: tepà, 'I smell'). nfw 'the breath, the air' is the sail (P5, approximate), the sign of wind and breath, with w and a stroke. pr 'which comes forth' is the participle of pri (house, r, legs), agreeing with nfw; prt, with t, agrees with the feminine mḥyt. m fnḏ·k 'from your nose': fnḏ is the nose sign with its stroke. mḥyt 'the north wind' is the sign mḥ (V22, approximate), the wick ḥ as complement, two reeds y, t and the sail. m mwt·k 'from your mother' (vulture mwt, t, ·k). The cool north wind of Egypt is the breath of life; it comes from the sun and from the sky.

sentences.i: May you glorify my spirit; may you make divine the Osiris, my ba.
sentences.n: sꜣḫ·k 'may you glorify' is the bolt s, the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ as complement, the papyrus roll and ·k: the sḏm·f of sꜣḫ 'make (someone) an ꜣḫ, glorify', the causative of ꜣḫ, used for a wish. ꜣḫ·i 'my spirit' is the ibis with its stroke, a squatting man holding a flail (approximated) and ·i: the ꜣḫ, the dead as a shining and effective spirit. nṯri·k is the flag nṯr with t (for ṯ) and r as complements, two strokes y, the roll and ·k: nṯri 'be divine', here with an object, 'make divine'; the sense follows the parallel sꜣḫ·k ꜣḫ·i, but nṯri is a verb of quality and the use is not certain (Budge: 'make strong'). Wsir is the low seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye with a stroke. It is taken as the dead man himself, 'the Osiris', with bꜣ·i 'my ba' (the jabiru bꜣ, with the small pot before it in the type, and ·i) in apposition; Budge takes Wsir as an address to the god, 'thou Osiris'. ꜣḫ and ba are two of the forms in which the dead live on.

sentences.i: Praise to you, at rest, O lord of the gods, and exaltation to you for your wonders!
sentences.n: dwꜣ tw 'praise to you' as in line 2, with the same doubt over the construction, split from one group of Budge's; the star is printed as a six-rayed asterisk. ḥtp 'at rest' (offering table, t, p) is taken as the stative, 'being at rest, having set', with its ending unwritten; Budge supplies '[in]' before it. nb nṯrw 'lord of the gods', an address. sqꜣ tw 'exalting you': sqꜣ 'make high, exalt', the causative of qꜣi 'be high', is the bolt s and the hill-slope q with a man raising both arms and a flat bar with a small tuft (approximated as Aa13; not read) as classifiers, the ꜣ unwritten; tw (t and the curl w) is the pronoun object. Budge prints the two as one word, seqa-tu, and takes it as passive ('thou art exalted'); they are split here, built like dwꜣ tw. m biꜣwt·k 'for your wonders': biꜣwt is a sledge carrying a box with an animal head on top (the sign biꜣ, U16, approximate), t and plural strokes, the plural of biꜣyt 'wonder, marvel', and ·k. The hymn turns to the sun at evening.

sentences.l: may-shine · you · rays · upon · breast · my · like · the-day
sentences.i: May you shine with rays upon my breast, as by day.
sentences.n: Two words of the same root stand side by side. The first is the pierced hide st (F29), t, w, the sun with hanging rays (approximate), a stroke and ·k: taken as a verb, the sḏm·f of wish, 'may you shine, send out rays', a verb made from the noun stwt and spelled like it. The second, stwt 'rays' (hide st, w, the rays and a stroke), is the noun, used as the means: 'shine (with) rays'. Budge too reads a verb and a noun ('shine thou [with thy] beams'). ḥr šnbt·i 'upon my breast' (šnbt as in line 2, now with ·i). mi hrw 'like the day': mi 'like' is the milk-jug in its net; hrw 'day' is the sun with a stroke. Budge gives 'daily' for the two words together; 'as by day' takes them as written. Ani asks to be lit by the sun even as it goes down.

sentences.i: — the Osiris, the scribe who reckons the god's offerings of all the gods, overseer of the Double Granary of the lords of Abydos,
sentences.n: Ani is named with his titles, in apposition to the 'my' of the line before: these are the words of the man himself. Wsir (low seat Q2, approximate, over the eye) and sš 'scribe' (the palette). ḥsb 'reckon, count' is an oval with a small ring (approximated as Aa2) over a flat bar with a tuft (approximated as Aa13), taken as the word-sign of ḥsb with a classifier; sš ḥsb is the 'scribe who reckons', the accountant. ḥtp-nṯr 'the god's offerings' joins two of Budge's words: the offering table ḥtp with t and p, then the flag nṯr with the seated god; here the flag is written after ḥtp, in the order of reading. n nṯrw nbw 'of all the gods'. imy-r 'overseer' is the hoe mr alone (U6), which writes the title imy-r, 'he who is in the mouth', the man whose word is obeyed; Budge reads mer. šnwty 'the Double Granary' is two domed silos on a platform (the sign šnwt, O51, approximate) with t and two strokes for the dual (Budge: śenti, 'the granary'): the store of temple grain. n nbw ꜣbḏw 'of the lords of Abydos': ꜣbḏw is the Abydos emblem, a wig on a pole with plumes (R17, approximate), with the town sign; the lords of Abydos are its gods.

sentences.n: wnn-nfr 'Wennefer' (Budge: Un-nefer), 'he who is (always) perfect', is the hare wn over two water-lines, the heart-and-windpipe nfr and the seated god, as in the hymn to Osiris on Plate 2. ḥr-ꜣḫty 'Horakhty' is spelled out here: the falcon ḥr, the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, t, two strokes y and two flat dotted ovals (coded N18, approximate) as classifiers; Budge prints Ḥeru - χuti with a hyphen, and it is kept as one word. Osiris is given the sun's name: the two gods meet in the night. ꜥšꜣ ḫprw 'many of forms' and ꜥꜣ irw 'great of shapes' are adjective-and-noun phrases. ꜥšꜣ 'many' is the lizard with plural strokes; ḫprw 'forms' as in the hymn to Ra. ꜥꜣ 'great' is a lozenge-tipped rod (the column ꜥꜣ, O29, approximate) with U15 standing for the complement ꜥ and a flat bar with a tie; irw 'shapes, forms' is the reed i as complement, the eye ir, w, a standing wrapped figure, the roll and a stroke.

sentences.n: Budge prints χu-sen-tu as one group; it is split here into the verb with its suffix and tw 'you'. The verb is a bent arm (coded D41, approximate; the arm holding a flail, the sign ḫw, is probably meant) with the placenta ḫ and the chick w as its complements, and a knotted upright (coded T3, approximate) as classifier, then ·sn 'they' (bolt s, water n, plural strokes): ḫw 'protect, guard', the sḏm·f of ḫwi, with the arm read ḫw as in the published parts. Budge gives 'they glorify'; both his reading and the signs are doubtful. ·sn refers to the gods of the line before. tw (t and w) is the pronoun object. ḥtp·k 'you set' is a sḏm·f standing as a clause of time, 'when you set'. m nwt 'in Nut': nwt is written with water n and the town sign, as in the hymn to Ra. At sunset the sun enters the body of the sky-goddess.

sentences.l: brighten · you · the-Two-Lands · with · fine-gold(?)
sentences.i: and you brighten the Two Lands with fine gold(?).
sentences.n: sḥḏ·k 'you brighten' is the bolt s, a knotted upright taken as the mace ḥḏ (T3, approximate) with the cobra ḏ as complement, the sun with hanging rays and ·k: the causative of ḥḏ 'be bright', a sḏm·f. Budge reads seḥet'-k. tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt, is the land sign written twice, with no ending written. The last word's first sign is coded M21 (approximate and doubtful), a tall thin stem with a hooked tip and a small loop at its foot; then the bead-collar of gold, a small circle and plural strokes. Budge reads smu and gives 'smu metal'. The stem with a hooked head is taken here as the sceptre that writes ḏꜥm, as in the hymn to Osiris on Plate 2, where ḏꜥm 'fine gold' has the same collar and grains; read ḏꜥm, with that doubt. If the sign is the plant sm (M21) it is coded as, the word is Budge's smw, not otherwise known as a metal; Budge reads smu on Plate 2 too, where the first sign is a staff. The setting sun lights the land below with the colour of gold.

sentences.i: Those who lie (in death) stand up to look upon you;
sentences.n: sḏryw 'those who lie down' is the bolt s, a bundle-like sign taken as ḏr (M36, approximate) with r as complement, two reeds y and a standing four-footed animal with a curled tail, perhaps a lion (approximated as E22), with a stroke: the plural participle of sḏr 'lie down, spend the night', a name for the dead (Budge: st'eriu, 'the dead'). ꜥḥꜥ 'stand up' is the mast-like sign ꜥḥꜥ, U15 where the arm ꜥ is read as complement, and the walking legs: the stative after its subject, with its ending unwritten, 'are standing up'. r mꜣꜣ 'to see': the eye with the sickle mꜣ over it, and two vultures ꜣ. Then water n and ·k: Budge prints maa-nek as one group, and it is split here into mꜣꜣ and n·k 'to you'. Where an object pronoun is expected (mꜣꜣ·k 'seeing you'), the papyrus has n·k; the same comes in line 5. Either the n is a later way of joining the object, or the verb is mꜣn, a later spelling of 'see'; either way the sense is 'to look upon you'. At the sunset the dead below rise to greet the god.

sentences.l: you · eternity · everlastingness
sentences.i: You are eternity and everlastingness.
sentences.n: ntk 'you' is the independent pronoun (water n, t, the basket k): ntk N, 'you are N', is a sentence with no verb. nḥḥ 'eternity' is the wick ḥ twice with the sun-disk between them as classifier of time, the water n of the word unwritten, as on Plate 2; ḏt 'everlastingness' is the cobra ḏ, t and the land sign. The two words stand side by side with no 'and': nḥḥ is time that comes round again and again, like the sun, ḏt time that stays, like Osiris; the god is both.

glossary.nfr: nfr — beautiful, good, perfect (adjective; follows its noun; verb 'be good'); also beauty, goodness (noun m.)
glossary.·ti: ·ti — you (2nd person singular ending of the stative: "you are …, you have …"; written ·tw here) · also written ·ṯi, with the tethering rope ṯ and the reed (the older spelling) · also 3rd person feminine singular ending of the stative: 'she, it is …' (written ·ṯi, as in sšw·ṯi 'it is emptied') · the 3rd feminine singular ending also written ·tw (rs·ti 'she is awake')
glossary.itrty: itrty — the Two Shrines, the national shrines of Upper and Lower Egypt, standing for the gods of the whole land (noun f., dual; Budge: àterti, 'the two regions')
glossary.nb: nb — lord, master, possessor (of); (adjective, after a noun) every, all
glossary.psḏ: psḏ — to shine, appear in light (verb)
glossary.psd: psd — to move (?) (verb; written with a leg as classifier; the word is not known otherwise; Budge: peṭes, pest) · back, backbone (noun m.; Budge: pesṭ, 'backbone')
glossary.mwt: mwt — mother (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: to die (verb; often written mt, without the w; Budge: mit) · mwtw 'the dead' (noun m. plural)
glossary.ḫꜥ: ḫꜥ — to appear in glory, rise (verb; of a king on his throne, a god, the sun) · also ḫꜥw, appearings, glorious appearances; crowns (noun m. plural; Budge: χāāu)
glossary.ir: ir — to do, make (lemma iri) · a second word of the same spelling: the particle ir "when, if" at the head of a clause (ir ꜥq·i "when I entered"), here apparently also bringing in a question ("do you know …?") · also "as for" (particle; ir with a noun puts that noun first as the topic) · also irt, what is done, deeds (noun f.; from iri 'do'; irt·k 'your deeds')
glossary.sḏm·n·f: sḏm·n·f — the n of the sḏm·n·f, marking a completed action ("I have …", "I …ed") (verb form; written between the verb and its suffix)
glossary.nwt: nwt — Nut, the sky-goddess, mother of the sun and of Osiris (god's name; Budge: Nut) · a second word of the same spelling: bonds, wrappings (?) (noun f. plural; Budge: netu) · a third word (?): a weapon or tool (noun f.; doubtful; Budge: nut(?))
glossary.nyny: nyny — to greet, welcome (verb); greeting, the gesture of welcome (noun)
glossary.ḥpt: ḥpt — door-post, jamb (?) (noun; plural ḥptw; sense not secure; Budge: ḥeptu) · a second word of the same spelling: to embrace, clasp (verb; written with the two embracing arms)
glossary.mꜣꜥt: mꜣꜥt — truth, right order (maꜥat) · also Maat, the goddess of truth and right order (god's name; the seated goddess with the feather)
glossary.tr: tr — then, now, pray (enclitic particle that presses a question) · a second word of the same spelling: time, season (noun m.; dual trwy 'the two times', morning and evening)
glossary.mr: mr — canal, channel, pool (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: to be ill, sick; sickness (verb, noun)
glossary.dsds: dsds — Desdes, a lake of the sky (place name, noun; Budge: Ṭes-Ṭes)
glossary.sbiw: sbiw — rebel, the rebel serpent, enemy of the sun-god (noun m.; from sbi 'rebel'; Budge: Sebàu)
glossary.ḫr: ḫr — to fall (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to, near, with (preposition; of persons) · also 'before' (ḫr nṯrw 'before the gods') · a third word: the particle ḫr, which brings in a further case or a consequence (?) (particle; sometimes written ẖr) · also 'from' (of persons: ḫr s nty·f ḫr·f 'from the man with whom it is')
glossary.ꜥ: ꜥ — arm, hand (noun; dual ꜥwy "the two arms") · a second word of the same spelling: state, condition (noun)
glossary.qꜣs: qꜣs — to bind, tie up (verb; stative 'bound')
glossary.ḥsq: ḥsq — to cut off (verb; written with the knife as classifier; perhaps also of cutting grain, reaping (?); Budge: ḥesq)
glossary.ṯst: ṯst — vertebra, backbone (noun f.; from ṯs 'tie'; Budge: θest, 'the vertebræ')
glossary.wnn: wnn — to be, exist (verb; wn·n·i "I have been"; n wn "there is not") · also wnnt, 'what exists' (participle, feminine: 'that which is')
glossary.sk: sk — to wipe, sweep (verb); perhaps also to drag, tow (?) (sense uncertain; Budge's 'toweth') · a second word of the same spelling: to perish (verb; skt after tm 'not perishing'; the Imperishable Stars iḫmw-sk are 'those who do not know perishing')
glossary.pḥ: pḥ — to reach, arrive at, attain (verb)
glossary.sw: sw — he, him, it (3rd person masculine singular dependent pronoun)
glossary.stꜣ: stꜣ — to drag, draw, haul (verb; of hauling a sledge or towing a boat)
glossary.sḏm·tw·f: sḏm·tw·f — the tw of the sḏm·tw·f, the passive or impersonal form ("one …", "… is done") (verb form; written after the verb, before its suffix)
glossary.šmꜥ: šmꜥ — the South, Upper Egypt (noun m.; Budge: qemāu, his old value for the sign) · plural nisba šmꜥyw, 'those of the south'
glossary.mḥtt: mḥtt — north (noun); northern (nisba adjective, feminine) · also mḥty, the masculine 'northern' (nisba adjective) · plural nisba mḥtyw, 'those of the north'
glossary.imntt: imntt — the West, the realm of the dead · plural nisba imntyw, 'those of the west'
glossary.iꜣbtt: iꜣbtt — the east, the eastern quarter where the sun rises (noun f.) · also eastern (nisba adjective, feminine, after a feminine noun: ꜣḫt iꜣbtt 'the eastern horizon') · plural nisba iꜣbtyw, 'those of the east'
glossary.pꜣwty: pꜣwty — the Primeval One, 'he of the primeval time' (noun m., epithet of a creator god; Budge: pautti)
glossary.ḫprw: ḫprw — forms, manifestations, ways of coming into being (noun m., plural; from ḫpr 'become')
glossary.wdi: wdi — to put, place, cast; to inflict (verb)
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.bꜥḥ: bꜥḥ — to flood, inundate, overflow (verb); the flood, inundation (noun m.)
glossary.sgr: sgr — to silence, make quiet (verb; causative of gr "be silent") · also the noun sgrw 'silence, stillness'
glossary.wꜥ: wꜥ — one; (as a noun) one (of), someone
glossary.imytw: imytw — between, among (preposition; from the nisba imy 'which is in'; Budge: àmt)
glossary.ḏw: ḏw — evil, bad; an evil deed (adjective, noun; written with the mountain ḏw) · also mountain (noun m.; plural ḏww 'mountains')
glossary.pḥrr: pḥrr — to run (verb); pḥrry 'runner, one who runs' (noun m.; Budge: peḥreri)
glossary.nbi: nbi — to fashion, mould, as a craftsman does (verb)
glossary.psḏt: psḏt — the Ennead, the company of nine gods (noun f.; psḏt nṯrw 'the Ennead of the gods'; Budge: paut)
glossary.ḫnp: ḫnp — to take, snatch away, draw out (?) (verb)
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who"
glossary.pri: pri — to go out, come forth (verb)
glossary.npt: npt — flooded land (?) (noun f.; Budge: nept)
glossary.tpi: tpi — to breathe in, inhale (?) (verb; Budge: tepà)
glossary.nfw: nfw — breath, wind (noun; written with the sail, which also writes ṯꜣw 'wind, breath')
glossary.mḥyt: mḥyt — the north wind (noun f.; the sail as classifier; Budge: meḥit) · also written short, mḥw (?)
glossary.sꜣḫ: sꜣḫ — to glorify, make (someone) an ꜣḫ, an effective spirit (verb; causative of ꜣḫ); sꜣḫw 'glorifications', the recitations that do this for the dead (noun, plural)
glossary.ꜣḫ: ꜣḫ — spirit, the glorified and effective dead (noun; written with the crested ibis) · also glory, effective power (noun m.) · also glorious, effective (adjective) · also to be glorious, be effective, be an effective spirit (verb) · also ꜣḫt, what is effective or useful, a benefit (noun f.) · also ꜣḫ n, to be of use to, serve, benefit (someone) (verb)
glossary.nṯri: nṯri — to be divine (?) (verb of quality) · also, with an object, to make divine (?)
glossary.bꜣ: bꜣ — ba, soul; the Ram, the ba-ram of Mendes (noun) · a second word of the same spelling: to hack open, break open (?) (verb; written like the word for the ba, with a knife as classifier; the sense is doubtful; Budge: ba, 'pass through')
glossary.sqꜣ: sqꜣ — to make high/loud (causative of qꜣi)
glossary.biꜣyt: biꜣyt — wonder, marvel (noun f.; plural biꜣwt)
glossary.stwt: stwt — rays, beams of light, esp. of the sun (noun f. plural; Budge: satetu) · a second word of the same spelling: meaning uncertain (?), written with a mummy-shaped classifier of images, perhaps from twt 'image' (noun) · also to shine, send out rays (?) (verb, spelled like the noun stwt)
glossary.mi: mi — come! (the imperative that serves the verbs of coming, iwi and ii; in later copies written with the owl m and the forearm ꜥ, as if mꜥ, with the walking legs) · a second word of the same spelling: like, as (preposition)
glossary.hrw: hrw — terror, dread · a second word of the same spelling: day (noun; plural hrww)
glossary.ḥsb: ḥsb — to reckon, count; sš ḥsb "accounting scribe" (verb)
glossary.ḥtp-nṯr: ḥtp-nṯr — god's offerings, the offerings of a temple (noun)
glossary.imy-r: imy-r — overseer, 'he who is in the mouth' (title, noun m.; the nisba imy of the preposition m with rꜣ 'mouth'; stands before the thing overseen)
glossary.šnwt: šnwt — granary (noun f.; dual šnwty 'the Double Granary')
glossary.ꜣbḏw: ꜣbḏw — Abydos, the holy city of Osiris (place name; Budge: Àbṭu) · a second word of the same spelling: the abdju-fish (noun; a fish that swims before the sun's bark)
glossary.mri: mri — to love, wish, desire (verb; relative form mrrt·f, mrt·f 'what he loves, what he desires')
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.ḏt: ḏt — everlastingness, time as unchanging permanence (noun f.; paired with nḥḥ) · a second word of the same spelling: body, person (noun f.)
glossary.wnn-nfr: wnn-nfr — Wennefer, 'he who is (always) perfect', a name of Osiris (god's name; Budge: Un-nefer)
glossary.ꜥšꜣ: ꜥšꜣ — many, numerous, much (adjective; the lizard sign) · multitude, the many (noun; with a suffix, 'its many (parts)'; Budge: āśt)
glossary.ꜥꜣ: ꜥꜣ — great (adjective); (adverb) here, hither · a second word of the same spelling: donkey, ass (noun) · a third word of the same spelling: door, door-leaf (noun; iry-ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper") · also greatly, very (adverb, after an adjective or participle: ḥsy ꜥꜣ 'greatly favoured') · dual ꜥꜣwy 'the two doors, the double door' (noun; written with the door-leaf twice)
glossary.irw: irw — form, shape, appearance (noun m.; from iri 'do, make')
glossary.ptḥ: ptḥ — Ptah, the creator-craftsman god of Memphis (god's name; Budge: Ptaḥ)
glossary.skr: skr — to bury (verb; meaning uncertain) · a second word of the same spelling: Sokar, the falcon god of the Memphite cemetery, drawn on a sledge, made one with Osiris (god's name; Budge: Seker) · also skry, the bark of Sokar (?) (noun)
glossary.iwnw: iwnw — Heliopolis, the sun-cult city (Budge: Annu)
glossary.šṯyt: šṯyt — the Shetayt, the shrine of the god Sokar (place name, noun f.; Budge: śeθit)
glossary.ḫnm: ḫnm — to smell; to be joined with (verb); here, doubtfully, as a noun "companion, friend"
glossary.ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ: ḥwt-kꜣ-ptḥ — Memphis ('Mansion of the ka of Ptah'; Budge: Het-ka-Ptah)
glossary.pw: pw — this, that (demonstrative, after its noun); 'it is' in nominal sentences (A pw 'it is A') · a second word of the same spelling: who? what? (interrogative pronoun; pw tr 'what then?')
glossary.sšm: sšm — image, figure (noun) · also procedure, the way a thing is done · also to lead, guide (verb); guide, leader (participle used as a noun)
glossary.dwꜣt: dwꜣt — the Duat, the underworld through which the sun and the dead pass by night (noun f.; place name; Budge: Ṭuat)
glossary.ḫwi: ḫwi — to protect, guard, keep safe (verb)
glossary.·sn: ·sn — they, them, their (3rd person plural suffix pronoun)
glossary.ꜣst: ꜣst — Isis, wife of Osiris and mother of Horus (goddess's name, written with the seat sign; Budge: Àuset)
glossary.sḥr: sḥr — to drive away, remove (verb; Budge: seḥeri, 'dispel')
glossary.ḏꜣyw: ḏꜣyw — opponents, adversaries (noun m. plural; from ḏꜣi 'cross, oppose'; Budge: t'ai)
glossary.rꜣ: rꜣ — mouth; utterance, spell (noun; rꜣ n … "spell for …", the heading of a chapter) · also 'opening, door' (noun; rꜣ n 'the door of')
glossary.rdi: rdi — to give, put, place; with a sḏm·f, to cause, let (verb; di·f pr·i "he let me come forth")
glossary.sḥḏ: sḥḏ — to make bright, illuminate (causative verb; from ḥḏ 'be bright')
glossary.sḏr: sḏr — to lie down, spend the night (verb; Budge: st'er)
glossary.ꜥḥꜥ: ꜥḥꜥ — to stand, stand up (verb); standing-place, stand, support (noun; plural ꜥḥꜥw) · also ꜥḥꜥ·n 'then', the auxiliary that opens a narrative sentence
glossary.itn: itn — the disk of the sun, the Aten (noun)
glossary.ntk: ntk — you (independent pronoun, 2nd person masculine singular; ntk N 'you are N', a sentence without a verb)
glossary.nḥḥ: nḥḥ — eternity, endless recurrence of time (noun m.; paired with ḏt)
